why: validate() returns at once for a non-dict schema, so for additionalProperties=True both paths accept every extra key; the isinstance check is redundant.
continue is the last statement of the oneOf loop body, so falling through to the next iteration is exactly what it does.
BASE['kind'] is replaced by the pinned enum in _base() for every schema; the entry only documents the envelope and is never used to validate.
after seek(-1, SEEK_END) exactly one byte remains, so read(1) and read(2) return the same byte.
Path.glob on a missing directory yields nothing, so the early return only skips a no-op.
The number only truncates the value echoed in the rejection's `got` field; no consumer parses it, and pinning the exact cut would make the test brittle against a cosmetic change.
Same as the notMatch echo: the slice length is diagnostic detail in `got`, not a contract any caller reads.
_obj() stores a None shape only when the caller passed none, and validate() tests the stored value for truth before dispatching, so the extra dict entry is inert.

Every falsy stamp (None, empty string, 0, False) raises ExecError from _iso2epoch, which the same function catches and answers 0.0 — so skipping the guard and falling through produces the identical value. The guard is defensive, not behavioural.
